quiz.title: Unit 7 LEQ: Responses to the Great Depression
quiz.headline: Responses to the Great Depression
quiz.prompt: Evaluate the similarities and differences in how the governments of the United States and Germany responded to the Great Depression between 1929 and 1939.
quiz.instructions: Develop an argument in one organized essay. Include a thesis, contextualization, specific evidence, and historical reasoning. This is untimed practice in AP long-essay format, not a full exam simulation.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice. Rubric categories follow the structure of the College Board's AP history rubrics; scoring here is your own self-assessment, not an official score.

responseFields.label: Optional outline
responseFields.prompt: Plan your claim, context, evidence, and reasoning before drafting.
responseFields.help: Optional planning notes; the essay is the required response.

responseFields.label: Essay response
responseFields.prompt: Write the full essay. Make the line of reasoning visible and explain why each example supports the claim.
responseFields.help: Informational word count only. No timer or automatic grading.

rubric.label: Thesis
rubric.guidance: Responds to the prompt with a historically defensible thesis or claim that establishes a line of reasoning.

rubric.label: Contextualization
rubric.guidance: Describes a broader historical context relevant to the prompt: developments before, during, or continuing after the period.

rubric.label: Evidence
rubric.guidance: 1 point: provides at least two specific historical examples relevant to the prompt. 2 points: uses specific and relevant examples to support an argument in response to the prompt.

rubric.label: Analysis and reasoning
rubric.guidance: 1 point: uses comparison, causation, or continuity and change to frame or structure the argument. 2 points: demonstrates a complex understanding, for example by explaining multiple causes, weighing similarities and differences, or using evidence to qualify or modify the argument.

scaffold.label: Claim
scaffold.text: Answer the prompt and preview your line of reasoning.

scaffold.text: Describe a broader development before or during the period.

scaffold.label: Reasoning
scaffold.text: Structure the essay around the reasoning process and qualify your claim.

quiz.modelResponse:
After the First World War, many economies relied on loans from the United States, and when the New York stock market crashed in 1929, those loans stopped and trade collapsed. Germany, which was already burdened by war debts and the memory of hyperinflation in 1923, suffered some of the worst unemployment in the world, and by 1932 about six million Germans were out of work. In the United States, unemployment reached about a quarter of the workforce by 1933.

The governments of the United States and Germany were similar in that both expanded state control of the economy to fight unemployment, but they differed because the New Deal aimed at relief and reform within a democracy while Nazi Germany directed the economy toward rearmament and rejected democratic limits.

Both governments used public works and government direction to put people to work. In the United States, Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal created the Civilian Conservation Corps and the Works Progress Administration, which employed millions in building roads, bridges, and parks. In Germany, the Nazi government that took power in 1933 funded public works, including the autobahn highways, and sharply increased spending on the military. Both showed that governments were willing to take a larger role in the economy than they had before the Depression.

The differences were also significant. The New Deal sought to relieve distress and prevent a repeat of the crash through reforms such as bank deposit insurance and the Social Security Act of 1935, while leaving private property and elections in place. Nazi economic policy was designed to prepare for war and to reduce dependence on imports. The government directed industry under the Four-Year Plan of 1936, suppressed labor unions, and persecuted Jews and other groups, who were forced out of jobs. German unemployment fell mainly because of rearmament and conscription, not because of reforms meant to make the economy fairer.

The results also differed. The United States recovered slowly and still had high unemployment in 1938, but it preserved democratic government. Germany reduced unemployment faster but did so through policies that led toward war.

In conclusion, both governments expanded their economic role, but the United States did so to relieve hardship within a democratic framework, while Nazi Germany did so to build a militarized, authoritarian state.

modelNotes.label: Contextualization
modelNotes.text: The first paragraph describes the stock market crash, the end of American loans, and Germany's earlier economic troubles.

modelNotes.label: Thesis
modelNotes.text: The thesis names a similarity and a difference and gives a reason for each.

modelNotes.label: Evidence
modelNotes.text: The CCC, the WPA, deposit insurance, the Social Security Act, the autobahn, rearmament, and the Four-Year Plan are specific and used in the comparison.

modelNotes.label: Analysis and reasoning
modelNotes.text: The essay compares aims, methods, and results, and qualifies the American recovery by noting continued unemployment in 1938, which shows complexity.

quiz.alternateModel: A different strong essay could compare the United States with the Soviet Union, arguing that both expanded government planning but that the Soviet Five-Year Plans replaced markets entirely while the New Deal worked within them.
commonErrors: Describing each government's policies in separate paragraphs without comparing them.
Claiming the New Deal ended the Depression by itself.
Treating Germany's falling unemployment as proof of a healthy economy.
Ignoring the political differences between a democracy and a dictatorship.
